/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 04 November 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2694 (104)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4097 (276)
Baltic Panamax Index: 1894 (28)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1835 (-11)
Baltic Handysize Index: 1016 (2)
CAPESIZE
The Capesize market made a positive move on Wednesday, with the BCI 182 5TC climbing by $2,511 to $37,162. The Pacific appeared to have found a floor, with C5 nudging up by $0.465 to $13.690, while the Atlantic continued to firm, pushing C3 up by $1.065 to $36.955. Activity in the Pacific was relatively quiet, with only one miner active in the market. The miner was said to have been bidding around $12.40 earlier in the day against offers in the mid-$13s, seemingly content to sit back and wait. Operators, however, were picking up the slack as improving bids encouraged activity, with one reportedly paying $13.50 before another followed at $13.75, providing a more positive indication of the market. The focus was firmly on South Brazil and West Africa to China, where a burst of activity followed a sluggish start to the week. Around 8–10 fixtures were reported, with C3 bids starting the day around $35.50 against offers near $36.50-$37.00. Fixtures were subsequently concluded in the $36.00–$36.50 range, with last done said to be $37.00 for early December dates. The North Atlantic also saw a healthy injection of fresh cargoes, supporting a stronger transatlantic market. The improved activity and firmer TA business lifted the C8 index by $5,125 to $37,375, adding further momentum to the broader Atlantic recovery.
PANAMAX
Market sources indicated a positive shift in sentiment across both basins, reflected in the P5TC rising by $258 to $17,049. An increase in both fronthaul and trans-Atlantic demand was highlighted, with several fixtures reportedly concluded above last-done levels. However, participants noted that the firmer rates being discussed appeared largely case-specific rather than indicative of a broader market move. Tonnage availability off the West Mediterranean was described as tighter, lending support to rates, while the North Continent remained comparatively well supplied, continuing to weigh on underlying market fundamentals. In the Pacific, Australian demand was said to remain active, while Indonesian activity was described as steady, reflected in the volume of reported fixtures. Market sources noted a wider bid-offer spread with Owners holding firmer to their ideas, particularly for modern units where employment opportunities appear more plentiful. The North Pacific was described as drawing support from the broader improvement in sentiment, with fundamentals appearing more balanced, although some sources noted a growing tonnage list. The Nea Tyhi (82,211 2009) open Putian prompt was reported to have fixed a Pacific round at $19,600, although no other details were heard.
SUPRAMAX
Another negative day across all index routes, with the 11TC average down a further $143 to $23,193. The backhaul dropped today, with news of the Sagittarius Honor (63,776 2025) fixed from North China to West Africa with steels/generals at $26,000 to Chinaland, whilst the BSI63 described vessel is not steels suitable. There were smaller drops elsewhere in the East including round voyages, whilst the Indian Ocean was harder hit with very limited activity evident from South Africa. The Atlantic continued its slow slump with rates gradually easing further, however there were some sources suggesting transatlantic rates from the US Gulf had maybe picked up a little, although this wasn’t widespread opinion. The Continent was much quieter, probably due to the upcoming Eisbein, and the Mediterranean was also subdued with limited fresh enquiry although sources said rates were generally unchanged. In the South there was talk of rates bottoming out from some, but there were few trades or rumours on which to base this on, and it seemed to be more Owners resisting lower bids for the timebeing.
HANDYSIZE
The market showed a mixed tone today, with the 7TC average edging up by $44 to close at $18,296. Across the Continent and Mediterranean changes were modest, but conditions remained healthy, with rates reported above last-done levels in most loading areas. The US Gulf adopted a more positive tone, supported by improving cargo flows and a shortage of prompt tonnage. In the South Atlantic, sources reported further easing in bid and offer levels as Charterers and Owners gradually lowered their expectations. Meanwhile, activity in the Pacific remained limited, although tonnage was tight and the cargo book healthy. The Infinity K (28,455 2008) open Nanjing on 14–17 November failed on subjects for a trip to West Coast India at $22,500. A 35,000-dwt vessel open Thailand was placed on subjects for a trip to Japan in the $18,000s, although further details were not disclosed.

Market Fundamentals
Transnet Declares Force Majeure

South Africa’s Transnet coal rail services along the Ogies–Ermelo–Vryheid route have been disrupted since 2 November, after Eskom power failures caused by severe weather suspended train movements on parts of the line, McCloskey reports. Transnet declared force majeure in a customer notice dated 3 November, and Eskom has yet to give a restoration time. In its latest investor report, Transnet railed 167.9 Mt of cargo in FY25/26 and is targeting 180 Mt in 2027.

Ukrainian Grain Exports

In its latest Grain and Feed Quarterly, the USDA Foreign Agricultural Service raised its forecast for Ukraine’s MY 2026/27 corn production by 1.7 Mt month-on-month to 33.5 Mt, citing higher yields in areas where harvesting has begun. Corn exports, however, were cut by 11.8 Mt to 10.2 Mt amid continued disruption to shipments and infrastructure. Minister of Agrarian Policy and Food, Taras Vysotskyi said Ukraine has secured enough grain storage bags to last through MY 2026/27.

Trading Commentary
Cape
Cape saw a strong session, with Nov and Dec rallying sharply through the morning before giving back some gains late. Nov opened at 35,250 before climbing to 36,500, with heavy volume around 36,000, last trading at 36,000. Dec strengthened from 35,500 to 37,350, with significant volume around 37,000–37,250, before easing to 36,750 late.
